newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican tortilla makers seek end to price controls.
newsitem.headline: Mexican tortilla makers seek end to price controls.

text.p: Mexican tortilla makers will present formal proposals to the government on Monday to end price controls on the corn-flour pancakes that are an essential element of the national diet.

Valentin Solis, adviser to the Mexico City branch of the Association of Mexican Tortilla Producers, told radio network Radio Red that tortilla makers sought a liberation of price controls for the food to avoid job losses and store closures.

Solis said rising costs, such as electricity, gas, rent and water, have forced tortilla makers to ask the government to end controls. He said he thought the current real market price for tortillas was between 2.50 and 2.90 pesos/kilo.
Tortilla prices, one of only two food products formally set by the government, are currently at 1.70 peso/kilo in Mexico City. Corn flour is the other product that has prices set by the government.
Prices for tortillas are slightly different in other states of the country. In northern U.S. border states, tortilla prices are already free to move to market supply and demand.

Mexico's Trade Ministry has hiked tortilla prices considerably in the last three years and officials have always said it is government policy to move to end controls on all products over the short to medium term.
Experts and corn traders believe the government will hike prices to around 2.00 pesos/kilo this winter and then move to erase all price controls by mid-year 1998.
